feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The candidate is the iteration 1 design (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, x = -0.02..0.02 at y = 0.04) with sensor_size 0.012. Iteration 1 is the best raced design at 75.97. Its progress was 0.29 on the s-bend, 0.16 on the oval and 0.115 on the slalom, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.065 on every track. Every change tried since then lowered the score: base_speed 1.2 with kd 0.1 (iteration 2, 50.60), kp 2.5 with kd 0.1 (iteration 3, 49.59), wider spacing (iteration 4, 57.85) and sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 5, 59.03). Changing kp did not move max_error, and the kd 0.1 runs lost progress on the s-bend and oval. Approving this candidate gives a race on the best known design, which is the safest score for this iteration. The race is most useful as a check that the iteration 1 result reproduces. If it does, the next iteration should test one lever at a time against it. If progress falls to about 0.16 on the s-bend, the 0.29 was seed-dependent and the design should be judged on the oval and slalom. Keep ki at 0 unless rms_error shows a steady offset.
requested_changes: If the race reproduces about 76 with progress near 0.29 on the s-bend, next test kd 0.15 with kp 2.0 and everything else unchanged. Iteration 1 showed kd 0.2 gave steering_oscillation 0.23 on the s-bend, and iteration 2 showed kd 0.1 cut progress, so 0.15 is the midpoint to check.

If progress on the s-bend falls to about 0.16 (the level of iterations 4 and 5), treat iteration 1 as seed luck and do not change the controller yet. Compare the s-bend and slalom line_loss_events against 1.95 and 2.0 before choosing the next lever.
Do not raise kp above 2.0 unless max_error changes. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5, kd 0.1) left max_error at 0.062 to 0.065, so kp is not reducing the error.
